resume: APL, family or social housing allowance: which one applies to you, the documents to prepare (including the rent certificate signed by the landlord) and applying to the Caf after a separation.
aQuoiCaSert: Housing benefits reduce the amount of your rent. There are three: the APL, linked to the home (a conventionné home, under an agreement with the State, like most HLM social housing); the family housing allowance (allocation de logement familiale, ALF), linked to your family situation, for example if you have children or receive family benefits; and the social housing allowance (allocation de logement sociale, ALS) for other cases. After a separation, each parent who takes a home can make their own application, calculated on their own income and new family situation.
quiEstConcerne: Tenants or subtenants of a decent home, occupied as their main residence in France.
APL: occupants of a conventionné home, whatever their family situation.
ALF: in particular people who receive family benefits or the AEEH, who have a dependent child under 21, or pregnant women living alone.
ALS: people who meet neither the APL nor the ALF conditions. Foreign nationals must have a valid residence permit.
aSavoir: APL, ALF and ALS cannot be combined. The amount depends on your income over the last 12 months (updated every 3 months), your assets (above €30,000), your rent, your family situation and where the home is: only the simulator of the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office) gives an estimate.
A subtenant must not be related to the main tenant or the landlord.
The benefit is paid on the 5th of each month. Entitlement starts on the 1st day of the month after the file is processed, about 2 months after the application: apply as soon as you move in.
If the Caf refuses, you have 2 months from the notification to challenge it; if that fails, mediation and then the amicable appeals board (commission de recours amiable) are possible.

Separation: declare it to the Caf. Each parent declares their own home and their own family situation; the amount is recalculated accordingly. Under shared residence, housing benefit is not shared between the parents.
